availability_provenance.note: Corrected 20 October 2026 for #139, applying Eleonora's ruling of 19 October 2026 on #132 (relayed on PR #134). The source is the New York Fed's launch press release of 17 October 2024: "The RDE will be updated around 10:00 A.M. Eastern Time on the third Thursday of each month, or on the first business day following a Federal Open Market Committee blackout period if the third Thursday of the month falls within the blackout period." It also says "The first RDE estimates, released today, include data as of Friday, October 11, 2024." Availability is declared at 12:00 New York time on the release day, the conservative reading of "around 10:00" and still before the 16:00 decision. A third Thursday inside an FOMC blackout (the second Saturday before a meeting through the day after it) moves to the first business day after the blackout; repo_liquidity.rde.release_day builds the meetings from the Board's calendar page saved in this repository, because the parent holds no meeting calendar at the pin. An estimate for date d is public at the first release whose data-as-of date is on or after d. Two as-of dates are recorded: Friday 11 October 2024 for the launch release, and Monday 5 October 2026 for the release of 15 October 2026 (the stored workbook's cover sheet, "Updated on October 5 for release on October 15"). A release with no recorded as-of date is assumed to carry data as of 10 days before its third Thursday, the larger of the two recorded gaps: a declared conservative lag, not a source (a marked question for Eleonora on PR for #139). The table starts at the estimate the launch release headlined (2024-10-09, the latest dated on or before 2024-10-11); the estimates before it are published apart as a labelled history series (rde_history.csv, "history, not public before 2024-10-17"), outside this declaration and read by nothing. The declared lag is the measured maximum of that rule over the rows read (scripts/extract_rde.py refuses any other).
availability_provenance.publication: Federal Reserve Bank of New York, Reserve Demand Elasticity, https://www.newyorkfed.org/research/reserve-demand-elasticity ; the Chart Data workbook at https://www.newyorkfed.org/medialibrary/Research/Interactives/Data/elasticity/download-data ; launch press release of 17 October 2024, https://www.newyorkfed.org/newsevents/news/research/2024/20241017

coverage: the NY Fed's estimate of the elasticity of the federal funds rate to reserves, with its 95% (2.5th to 97.5th percentile) and 68% (16th to 84th) intervals, about weekly estimate dates, latest-release vintage
nyfed_rde.limitation: An EXTERNAL CHECK on H7m goalposts 1 and 3: reported, never deciding (Eleonora, 19 October 2026); R and S stay the deciding benchmarks and nothing here is wired into a goalpost or a score. LATEST-RELEASE figures: the page serves only its latest workbook, so each value is the one in the release labelled in the vintage column, which may differ from the first print; earlier releases are not recoverable. The elasticity is the slope of the reserve demand curve, a pure number that is negative in the ample and scarce regions; the 50th percentile is the main estimate and a positive value is noise around zero. The estimate dates are about weekly (the sheet has no fixed weekday). The table starts at the estimate the launch release headlined (2024-10-09); the 634 earlier estimates (2010-01-20 to 2024-10-02) are the back history the launch carried, not a point-in-time series: they are published apart as a labelled history series, outside this declaration, and left out. The declared lag is read per panel row by the parent's rule at the measured worst case; repo_liquidity.rde.read is the exact, row-by-row reader. Estimates whose assigned release is after the parent's development end are withheld. Whether the RDE's definition of scarce reserves matches H7's kink is not checked. Phase 3 only; not in the published declaration.
nyfed_rde.provider: Federal Reserve Bank of New York

release_lag.note: Declared 20 October 2026 for #139 (first 19 October 2026 for #132) at the measured maximum and not above it: the longest gap from an estimate date to the day it is read as public under repo_liquidity.rde.release_for over the rows in the table, with availability at 12:00 New York time (scripts/extract_rde.py refuses any other value). An estimate is read at the first release whose data-as-of date is on or after its date, so the lag runs from a few days to the maximum; reading every estimate at the worst case is staleness on the safe side, not leakage.

nyfed_rde.reviewed_note: Structural-zero semantics are not applicable to an estimated elasticity; the empty declaration is not a finding.
